thread:
kai: Short follow-up: we didn't finalize the on-disk/remote serialization format for quant profiles. This matters for cross-runtime compatibility and canary rollbacks. Thoughts?

sara: Agreed important. current proto is ad-hoc JSON blobs with metadata, but we need a canonical schema + checksum + compatibility rules.

lee: Can we version the profile schema (v1, v2) and embed a self-describing header? That lets older runtimes refuse incompatible profiles gracefully.

kai: Yes. Proposal: header with fields: schema_version, model_hash, kernel_hints, checksum. Runtimes verify model_hash + checksum before applying.

violet: Also: profiles reference hardware-specific kernel hints (e.g., amx_fp8, cuda_int8_pack). How do we avoid sprawl? Suggest: separate profile layers: generic_quality -> layer_hints -> hw_overrides. Runtimes pick layers they understand.

runtime-bot: note: applying profile with unknown hw_overrides should fall back to generic_quality or fail safe.

lee: Example compact format sketch:
```
{
  "header": "quant-profile/1",
  "model_hash": "sha256:abcd...",
  "checksum": "sha256:ef01...",
  "layerset": "base+attn-scale-v2",
  "assets": ["scale-table.bin","calib.json"],
  "compat": ["redwood-runtime>=2.3","quant-adapter>=1.0"]
}
```

sara: We should standardize the checksum algorithm (sha256) and require signed manifests for enterprise/private installs (pkix signature). Ops needs to be able to audit who uploaded a profile.

kai: How to handle rolling back when new profile is bad? If we keep profile ids immutable and store last-good id per-endpoint, rollback is atomic: switch profile pointer. But we need migration tests so an old runtime can still read the profile.

violet: Compatibility testing: recommend a two-step canary: 1) static validation (schema + model_hash + checksum) 2) dry-run shadow apply on 1% traffic to collect delta metrics. If metrics exceed thresholds, auto-mark as bad.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary plan note: shadow apply gating requires no billing for shadow CPU/GPU time unless customer opted in.

lee: One subtlety: calibration artifacts. If a profile contains per-head scale tables generated on one GPU type, they may be suboptimal elsewhere. Profiles need optional per-hw recalibration hooks or portability metadata (scale_bias_range).

kai: Maybe pack portable calibrations plus hw-optimized assets. Runtimes choose best asset they support. Add a "portable_calib" block that can be recomputed at runtime to local format if needed.

sara: On the tooling side: add a profile_lint CI step that rejects: missing checksum, missing compat list, or per-layer mismatches with model shapes. This will cut down on runtime errors.

violet: Observability: emit events quant.profile.applied, quant.profile.rejected with reason, and include profile_id + manifest_checksum in logs. That ties into audit trail.

lee: Security: signing + revocation list. If a profile is found to cause degradation or security issue, we need an ability to mark it revoked and have runtimes refuse it even if checksum matches.

kai: Good point. Add a signed revocation list, fetched periodically by runtimes. Revocations should be instant for hosted but have a TTL for private installs. Document clearly.

runtime-bot: warning: large manifests (many assets) increase fetch latency. Prefer bundling small assets and remote pointers for large binaries.

ops-bot: Ops acceptance criteria request: 1) every profile must pass lint and be signed for production; 2) canary dry-run must show <1% quality delta vs baseline on seed prompts or auto-revert; 3) rollback must occur within 30s of detection.

sara: Action items I can take: profile schema PR + CI linter. ETA 3 days.

lee: I'll prototype header parsing and revocation check in runtime branch. ETA EOW.

violet: I'll draft the ops playbook for canary/dry-run + shadow billing opt-in. ETA EOW.

kai: I'll write the profile manifest spec and include examples for portable_calib and hw_overrides. ETA 2d.

ops-bot: [incident-bot] Reminder: if profile causes error-rate or latency spike > 2% during canary, auto-revert.

sara: One last Q: should we allow mutable profiles (hotpatch) or require immutability? Mutable is convenient but dangerous. I vote immutable + pointer swap.

lee: Immutable + pointer swap. Easier to reason about, deterministic audit trail.

kai: Agreed. I'll reflect that in the spec (profile_id immutable, endpoint has profile_pointer).

violet: No objections. Thanks all, will sync once PRs land.
